note: Each rule names the hub records it comes from. `match` is a substring of a claim quote in that record; clipcheck resolves it from index/records.jsonl at run time, so the quote shown is the hub's verbatim text. A rule whose provenance does not resolve says so.

rules.title: Size, rate, length and codec match the contract
rules.hint: Render at the contract's size, fps and length. Check the composition settings before changing content.

rules.title: The file says which colour space it is in
rules.hint: Tag the output (for Remotion: --color-space=bt709). An untagged file is decoded by guesswork and the palette shifts.

provenance.note: run here once: the untagged Remotion render decoded the accent as #43B589 instead of #4CC38A

rules.title: The first frame is not empty
rules.hint: Start with the first element already visible, or set a poster frame. Platforms take the thumbnail from early frames.

provenance.note: run here once: one clip opened on 7 empty frames

rules.title: No frame mid-clip without scene content
rules.hint: Overlap the outgoing and incoming scene, or hold one element through the cut. Check the exact frames listed.

provenance.note: run here once: three scene changes passed through a frame showing only an accent bar; a blind reviewer flagged it

rules.title: No run of frames that is nearly bare
rules.hint: Start the incoming scene earlier or let the outgoing one leave later, so the two overlap.

provenance.match: Decide what the viewer should notice first

rules.title: Only the contract's colours are on screen
rules.hint: Replace the listed colours with a palette colour or an opacity step of one. Greys for secondary text and panels count as extra colours.

provenance.note: run here once: a grey panel and grey secondary text cost the clip a rubric point

rules.title: Content stays inside the safe area
rules.hint: Move or shrink the element. Margins come from the contract; platform safe zones are larger at the bottom.

rules.title: Scene changes happen where the contract puts them
rules.hint: Retime the sequence so each scene starts at its contract time; a voiceover or caption track depends on it.

provenance.match: Decide what the viewer should notice first

rules.title: Moves decelerate instead of stopping dead
rules.hint: Give arrivals an ease-out. A move that ends at full speed reads as linear, the default look of generated motion.

rules.title: No long stretch with nothing moving
rules.hint: Add a secondary beat, or shorten the hold. The contract sets the limit.

provenance.note: no hub record quotes a hold limit yet; the contract sets it. An earlier version of this rule ignored slow wipes and an agent sped a wipe up to satisfy it

rules.title: Loudness and true peak are inside the contract range
rules.hint: Normalise with ffmpeg loudnorm to the contract target, then measure again with ebur128.

rules.title: Caption cues are short enough to read
rules.hint: Split the cue or slow it down: the contract sets lines, characters per line, characters per second and the shortest time on screen.

rules.title: Every string in the contract is in the project source
rules.hint: Add the missing string exactly as the contract writes it. Check for a changed character, a split across elements, or a line built by code.

provenance.note: run here once: both agents read an ambiguous brief differently and each lost a rubric point for copy

rules.title: Contract strings can be read on screen (advisory)
rules.hint: Open a frame and confirm the string is there and legible. Text reading from pixels misses small, coloured or monospace text; it is evidence, not proof.

provenance.note: run here: full-frame text reading missed two strings that were on screen in a clean clip, so this rule can only advise

rules.title: No numbers on screen that the contract does not list
rules.hint: A count-up shows values that are not true on the way to the real one. Reveal the figure instead of counting to it.

provenance.note: run here once: a counter animated through 54 and 112 on the way to 147, on a line reporting a verification result
